orchestrator_output.reformulated_query: Types and shapes of magnets and their uses
orchestrator_output.text_narration: Magnets come in many shapes, sizes, and types, each designed for specific uses. Broadly, magnets are grouped based on how they are formed and how long they keep their magnetic power. Magnets are mainly classified into natural magnets and artificial magnets. Natural magnets, like lodestone, are naturally occurring rocks that attract iron, but they have weak magnetic power and irregular shapes. Artificial magnets are human-made from materials like iron, nickel, or steel, and can be made very strong and shaped as needed. Artificial magnets are made in different shapes for different purposes. A bar magnet is a simple rectangular rod used in physics labs. A horseshoe magnet is bent like a U-shape to bring both magnetic poles close together for stronger pull. A cylindrical magnet is shaped like a rod or tube. A ball-ended magnet has spherical ends, often used in compasses and toys. Based on how long they retain magnetism, artificial magnets are divided into permanent and temporary magnets. Permanent magnets, like bar magnets, keep their magnetic property for a long time. Temporary magnets, like electromagnets made by passing electricity through a wire coil wrapped around an iron nail, act as magnets only when electric current flows. Different magnets are used everywhere in daily life. Ring magnets are used in speakers, bar magnets in scientific experiments, horseshoe magnets in heavy cranes to lift iron scrap, and electromagnets in electric bells and MRI machines in hospitals.
